answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to lock collateral in a protocol vault before it may attest or vote. The bond stays frozen until the agent crosses a verified-work ridge: a sustained record of peer-attested useful output. Only then does it receive a share of protocol nectar. Spinning up thousands of fake agents therefore demands a matching vault deposit for each sockpuppet, plus the time and cost to clear the same ridge, so attack capital scales linearly while slashing burns the locked funds if collusion is proven.
